text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The head of the State Tax Service Alexander Pochinok says companies failing to pay taxes will have to transfer some of their most liquid assets to the government.

- Ukrainian Industry and Energy minister Anatoly Minchenko strikes a deal with Azeri leaders which could lessen the country's dependence on Russian energy supplies and promote Ukraine as an important player on the world energy market.
- Rossiisky Kredit bank and the administration of the Kursk region in Central Russia have come to terms over the fate of Mikhailovsk ore mining and processing plant.
- The State Duma passes a law on free economic zones in Russia.
- Chechnya says it will turn to foreign donors if Russia fails to fulfil its promises of economic cooperation.
- A new Moscow exchange supposed to deal in municipal bonds holds its first trade session.
SEVODNYA
- The head of the State Tax Service Alexander Pochinok says a change in tax legislation will help collect taxes.
- The tax service and the Interior Ministry differ on figures for overall tax collection but both agree it is way below what it should be.
- Former Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin says the government will have to use commercial banks for its transactions at least till the end of 1997 before the Central Bank is able to take over.
- Czech automaker Skoda will supply 80 percent of car parts for a Skoda assembly line in Smolensk supposed to produce about 12.000 cars annually.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russians have to learn to live within their means if the economy is to get back into shape, says Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Sysuyev in an interview.
- Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov says the State Tax Service reports better tax receipts than they actually are.
- Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom's tax arrears are five times greater than its cashflow.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- Taxes will go down but control over their collection will be tightened, says Tax Service head Alexander Pochinok at a news conference.
- The railways ministry has worked out a programme to cut tariffs.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov, on a visit to the U.S., signs a $500 million five-year contract to introduce debit smart-cards in Moscow.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
